situation.summary: Carrier shift underway: Theodore Roosevelt left San Diego for an expected Middle East relief while Lincoln nears Hawaii homebound; two U.S. carriers stay on the Hormuz blockade. South China Sea pressure rose after a blocked Ayungin resupply, a Scarborough drill with a WZ-7 drone, and a U.S. condemnation — Hormuz remains shut.

flashpoints.title: Hormuz stalemate holds
flashpoints.text: Washington rejected Tehran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says it will not drop conditions (end hostilities, lift the port blockade, oil sanctions and frozen funds). The waterway remains largely closed; two U.S. carriers (George Washington, George H.W. Bush) stay on the CENTCOM blockade while Theodore Roosevelt deploys as expected relief.

src.title: USS Theodore Roosevelt Deploys From San Diego, USS Abraham Lincoln Near Hawaii

flashpoints.title: U.S. condemns Ayungin blocking; resupply still disrupted
flashpoints.text: After China Coast Guard and PLAN vessels obstructed a Sept 24 Philippine resupply to BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin), the U.S. embassy in Manila condemned 'dangerous blocking' and escalatory tactics that risked collision. Manila says three PLAN warships and five CCG vessels interfered; the RoRe mission was suspended.

src.title: US condemns China's dangerous maneuvers in Ayungin

flashpoints.title: Scarborough drill: WZ-7 drone and expanded-zone claim
flashpoints.text: PLA Southern Theater and China Coast Guard ran consecutive drills at Scarborough Shoal on Sept 27, publicly showcasing a Guizhou WZ-7 Soaring Dragon drone, KJ-500H AEW, Type 054A frigates and boarding rehearsals. Chinese state media claimed 'control' around Scarborough and Second Thomas now extends beyond 24 nautical miles.

src.title: China Claims Expanded Zone Around Scarborough Shoal, Deploys New Drone

flashpoints.title: Summit over; $14B arms package still held
flashpoints.text: The U.S.–China summit produced no public Taiwan breakthrough. Taipei says arming Taiwan remains an important U.S. interest; the ~$14B U.S. arms sale is still under review. Analysts note further U.S.–China meetings later in 2026 could keep the package delayed.

flashpoints.title: PLA day around Taiwan: 1 median-line crossing
flashpoints.text: Taiwan MND (6 a.m. Sept 27 to 6 a.m. Sept 28): 3 PLA aircraft sorties, 5 PLAN ships and 4 official ships around Taiwan. 1 of 3 sorties crossed the median line into Taiwan's northern ADIZ. ROC forces responded with CAP aircraft, navy ships and coastal missiles. Still routine gray-zone tempo, not a named large exercise.

flashpoints.title: Russian drones kill 7+ across Ukraine Sept 28
flashpoints.text: AP: round-the-clock Russian bombardment killed at least seven and wounded more than 80 on Sept 28, hitting homes, offices, gas stations, data centers and Kyiv's National Academy of Sciences. Ukrainian Air Force reported 165 attack/decoy drones overnight (112 downed/suppressed by 0700). Kyiv also claimed strikes on Russian defense plants and oil facilities.

src.title: Russian drones hammer apartments, offices and a cultural landmark in Ukraine, killing 7
Russia launches 165 drones at Ukraine on September 28

flashpoints.title: North Korea hypersonic and rocket tests
flashpoints.text: North Korea tested a new hypersonic-glide Hwasongpho-11Ma-1 variant on Sept 20 (two missiles from the Wonsan area; ranges reported ~440–600 km). On Sept 22 it tested upgraded 240 mm guided rockets claiming 100–115 km reach. Allied Freedom Edge drills (U.S.–ROK–Japan) had wrapped Sept 11.

flashpoints.title: Japan long-range missiles in Keen Sword
flashpoints.text: Japan plans to involve Ground Self-Defense Force Type-25 long-range surface-to-ship missiles in the October Keen Sword U.S.–Japan field exercise (information-sharing and launch procedures; no live firing planned). Part of Japan's counterstrike capability push.
